data_requests.item: Existing system/end-use demand, control and storage basis
where: site records: Existing actual compressor/system, critical end-use pressure and air quality, control/capacity mode, receiver volumes and location/coverage, peak magnitude/duration and interval, pressure differential, available compressor supply during events and replenishment/recovery time; source, units and comparable operating periods retained.

a walkdown: Only if an applicable question remains after reviewing existing records, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no mandatory new meter, field test, operating change or equipment replacement.
data_requests.how: A receiver/storage label anywhere is not this air system's coverage or sufficient capacity, and missing representation is not installed absence. Review actual demand patterns, controls and current receivers first; the appropriate strategy depends on quantity/quality and pressure requirements, event and refill timing and compressor/control characteristics. S11 printed43-44 does not endorse a universal gallons-per-cfm rule. A known compressor package is not excluded merely because its name mentions a dryer; helpers and known nonair machines are not air subjects. Acknowledge suitable existing coverage before additional work; no obligatory one-week logging, receiver installation, compressor stop or pressure change is authorized.

questions.decision_rule: Review actual system and critical end-use requirements, existing receiver coverage, pressure/demand/event and refill profiles and interacting compressor/control constraints with the responsible specialist. Short peaks or an extra unit starting are not by themselves an instruction to add storage. Suitable existing strategy or nonapplicability can be acknowledged; unresolved service, source, quantity, quality, pressure or timing remains a records question, not a sizing or vessel-safety approval.

typical_benefit.wording: Storage "may allow such a compressor to be turned off." No % stated.
typical_benefit.arc: 2.422x (category only) (IAC/ITAC browse page: 8,589 recommendations, 1.2 yr average payback, 46.5% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)
source_titles: S10: Compressed Air Tip #9, Compressed Air Storage Strategies (DOE/GO-102004-1965)
S24: DOE IAC/ITAC database: browse pages, download, schema document

questions.limits: IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers. Source review: S10 complete pp1-2 and S11 printed43-44/PDF48-49 make storage conditional on demand/quality/control and location/replenishment constraints; existing generic storage does not clear all systems. Pressure-vessel safety, relief, condensate/drain and maintenance constraints remain engineering responsibilities. No universal receiver volume or site savings is computed.
